title: General Hospital Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes Ran Mouri, Conan Edogawa, and Inspector Megure omitted by convention (pure observers/investigators with no causal edges of their own). Kept as an exception: Kogoro Mouri (p7) IS included as a person node, unlike the usual convention, because in this episode he is not a bystander detective but the mechanism's actual target -- he is deliberately drugged, gaslit into doubting his own sanity across three staged 'murders,' then knocked unconscious and framed with the murder weapon in hand; omitting him would delete the frame-up structure that is this episode's entire crime design. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. Multigraph: parallel typed edges between the same two nodes are expected (e.g. Shirai->dummy has three separate `stages_fake_murder_using` edges, one per staged night, plus later evidentiary edges). The old wiki-derived case file at cases/ep083_general_hospital_murder_case.json got the culprit/victim/suspect identities right but is otherwise a flattened summary: it collapsed the entire mirror/reflection staging mechanism, the cell-phone alibi relay trick, the sleeping-medicine/alarm-clock manipulation of Kogoro, the blackmail motive (Eto blackmailed Shirai over a bribed medical-school admission -- the bribed professor was Eto's own father), and named minor characters (nurses Kazumi Nakayama and Keiko Okita) into two generic clue blurbs and three flat 'knows' edges; it also mislabeled both nurses as undifferentiated 'suspects' despite the transcript giving them no motive or opportunity. case_type: murder.

attrs.false_alibi: claimed to have been in his own 2nd-floor north-ward room the whole time, on a phone call with an anonymous complainant, corroborated by nurse Okita hearing him talk while she delivered his charts and coffee

attrs.died_of: stab wound (two wounds total; the first was fatal, the second delivered afterward showed no vital reaction)
attrs.relationship_to_shirai: college classmate and fellow candidate for the retiring chief surgeon's position

attrs.unwitting_role: delivered Shirai's charts and coffee to his room at the time of the murder and spoke with him by voice, unknowingly corroborating his cell-phone relay alibi trick

attrs.circumstance: being forced to retire the following month, opening a position both Eto and Shirai wanted, which supplied the murder's motive
accepted a bribe years earlier from Shirai to secure his admission to medical school; being Eto's father is what let Eto learn of and exploit the bribe

spent three nights believing he witnessed real murders through his window (actually a mirror-trick reflection of a staged dummy), was dismissed as stress-hallucinating each time, then on the fourth night was drugged, had his room's curtains opened and alarm set to 11:30 by Shirai, rushed to the murder room upon 'witnessing' it again, was knocked unconscious, and woke with the murder weapon in his hand and Eto's real body nearby

attrs.note: its window, at the right angle after rain, acted as a mirror that reflected the storeroom/murder room across the way; fresh rain blotches on the glass, recently made each of the four nights, tipped Conan off to the trick

unused room with no curtains, diagonally positioned from Kogoro's room; housed the first-aid training dummy used to stage three fake murders, and was where Eto was actually killed on the fourth night, using the identical window-reflection staging
site of his false alibi -- a phone here was left connected on speaker to his cell phone so he could appear to be present and mid-conversation while actually across the building committing the murder

attrs.function: posed and reflected via the window-mirror trick to simulate three fake stabbings across three separate nights, priming Kogoro (and everyone around him) to believe he was hallucinating from stress

attrs.delivered_by: Keiko Okita, at the time of the murder
attrs.sugar_state: unused, despite Shirai's well-known sweet tooth
attrs.fingerprint_state: only Okita's fingerprints remain, on the handle; none of Shirai's are present anywhere on the cup
attrs.explanation: Shirai never drank it while committing the murder; afterward, to keep up appearances, he poured it out and rinsed the inside of the cup while still wearing the surgical gloves he'd used during the killing -- which erased any prints he might have left without adding new ones over Okita's

attrs.wound_detail: first stab was fatal; the second, delivered afterward, showed no vital reaction
attrs.staging_flaw: pressed into Kogoro's unconscious hand after the murder to transfer his fingerprints onto it and frame him -- the surface reading implicated Kogoro, not Shirai

objects.name: Blunt object used to knock out Kogoro

attrs.note: not yet disposed of when Shirai returned to his own room, which is why he kept his gloves on to rinse the coffee cup -- he could not risk leaving fingerprints on the weapon before disposing of it

attrs.given_to: Kogoro, under the guise of a normal nightly dose
attrs.purpose: kept him drowsy and compliant so he'd wake, groggy and unquestioning, exactly when the alarm and staged scene called for
guaranteed Kogoro would be awake and looking at the window at the exact moment of the murder

attrs.trick: just after 11:00, Shirai called his own cell phone from the phone in his room and left it on speaker, then carried the cell phone with him to the murder room; when Okita entered his room to deliver charts and coffee and spoke to the room's phone, he answered live via the cell phone from across the building, sounding exactly as if he were physically present the whole time

clues.desc: The coffee cup Okita delivered to Shirai's room carries only her fingerprints on the handle and none of his, even though he claims to have drunk from it and rinsed it himself -- if he had genuinely rinsed it bare-handed after drinking, some trace of his own prints should remain layered with or instead of hers.

The coffee's sugar was left completely untouched, despite Shirai's well-established sweet tooth -- inconsistent with him actually having been in the room to drink it at the time Okita says she spoke with him.

rushes in after witnessing the 'fourth murder' through his window
